mbm-0751.clue: I can get a tune going with two sticks and a kitchen chair.
mbm-0751.quote: Our son group practices until the last bus. When our claves rolled under the stove, my cousin tapped the rhythm with two wooden spoons. Now we bring them to every rehearsal.

mbm-0752.clue: I kept the little pink weight.
mbm-0752.quote: When my shoulder was ready for the big dumbbells again, I put the little pink one by the gym door. It’s a very good doorstop. Some days it’s still a very good weight.

mbm-0753.clue: I still have the photograph my towel took.
mbm-0753.quote: I asked my sister to photograph my first slalom run. She got my grin, the spray and a corner of the towel she was hiding behind. It’s my favorite picture of us both.

mbm-0754.clue: My grandfather washed the stopwatch before giving it to me.
mbm-0754.quote: I timed Grandpa’s first lap in thirty years. He did backstroke the whole way so he could see us cheering on the balcony. I forgot to stop the watch.

mbm-0755.clue: My good-luck charm has no business flying.
mbm-0755.quote: I dropped my toy penguin into the open pocket of my first flight bag. It rode along for my first solo. Now the penguin has more hours in the air than my brother.

mbm-0756.clue: I can tell the time by a paperback.
mbm-0756.quote: I read on the sunny side of our roof until the water tower’s shadow covers my knees. This summer I finally picked a mystery good enough to make me move the chair.

mbm-0757.clue: My sister packs a teaspoon for the slopes.
mbm-0757.quote: She handed me a spoonful of snow after I finished my first black run. We had forgotten the champagne and agreed this was better anyway.

mbm-0758.clue: I lift to the sound of a squeaky wheel.
mbm-0758.quote: The old gym fan squeaks once every three seconds. I use it to pace my curls. Somebody oiled it last Monday and six of us lost count together.

mbm-0759.clue: I save the chipped blue plates for Sundays.
mbm-0759.quote: Two weight plates in our gym came from my uncle’s garage. His thumbprint is still set in the blue paint. I put them on the bar when I’m lifting with him.

mbm-0760.clue: My quilt has its own front door.
mbm-0760.quote: I stitched our old apartment building into a blanket for Mum. Every window opens. She found the little felt cat behind ours before she found herself.

mbm-0761.clue: I know how far a tennis ball floats on the tide.
mbm-0761.quote: Our beach-cricket match stopped when the ball rolled into the surf. A little girl returned it with a sand dollar balanced on top. We made her captain on the spot.

mbm-0762.clue: My grand entrance involved a duck.
mbm-0762.quote: I finally stood up on both skis and saw a duck swimming right through my wake. Everybody cheered. The duck bowed its head for a fish and got all the credit.

mbm-0763.clue: I wrote my first record on a lunchbox.
mbm-0763.quote: My sister counted my reps on the lid with a grease pencil. The numbers polished off years ago. I still ask her to count if she’s in the gym.

mbm-0764.clue: I took a flower apart without picking it.
mbm-0764.quote: I had one crooked petal in the first flower I stitched for my aunt’s pollera. She turned the skirt in the light and called that the petal catching the breeze.

mbm-0765.clue: I buy the postcard before I look for the painting.
mbm-0765.quote: My little cousin picked a postcard of a white horse and sent me into the museum to find it. I spent an hour before I spotted the horse behind a much bigger boat.

mbm-0766.clue: I always wear the jacket with the bad pocket.
mbm-0766.quote: A coin fell through the lining in the middle of my first magic show. My best trick that day was making the whole front row listen to my elbow jingle.

mbm-0767.clue: I know who won by the smell of oranges.
mbm-0767.quote: We peel one orange for every strike. My first turkey left three long curls of peel on the scoring table. The janitor asked if we’d opened a fruit stand.

mbm-0768.clue: I have a tiny storm inside my computer.
mbm-0768.quote: I wanted my weather program to show more than numbers. Now a tiny pixel frog opens an umbrella when it rains. I keep hoping for a wet forecast.

mbm-0769.clue: I keep an extra chair at the arcade.
mbm-0769.quote: My grandma plays driving games standing up. The chair is for me, because she can make a single coin last all afternoon. She parks before she lets go of the wheel.

mbm-0770.clue: I throw a little to the left of the laundry.
mbm-0770.quote: Our first flying-disc goal was two shirts pinned to the line. My brother ducked through them to make the catch and came out wearing both sleeves. That one counted twice.

mbm-0771.clue: I keep a feather-shaped hole in my notebook.
mbm-0771.quote: I saw a kingfisher dive before I could sketch it. All I got was one blue streak, so I cut a little window in the page and held it up to the river.

mbm-0772.clue: I retired my lucky shoelace in public.
mbm-0772.quote: I threw my first strike with a borrowed shoe held shut by a neon shoelace. Our alley hung the lace from the counter like a championship banner. I signed the knot.

mbm-0773.clue: My best card has a bite missing.
mbm-0773.quote: Our hamster chewed the corner off my dragon card. I gave it a clear sleeve and promoted the hamster to dragon tamer. My friends still ask if he’s accepting apprentices.

mbm-0774.clue: I’ve sewn a whole weather report.
mbm-0774.quote: My sister sent me a scrap the color of the sky every Sunday for a year. The long gray strip across the middle is where we both got tired of rain.

mbm-0775.clue: I can hear the fifteenth hole from the snack bar.
mbm-0775.quote: A metal frog at our mini-golf course rings a bell if you putt through its mouth. Dad went through three buckets of balls just to make it ring on my birthday.
